hook: The quiet test pilot who became the first person to walk on the Moon.

pages.x: Neil Armstrong was born in 1930 near Wapakoneta, Ohio. He took his first airplane ride at six, and got his pilot's licence at 16, before he could drive a car.
He flew 78 combat missions as a navy pilot in the Korean War, and once had to bail out after a wire sliced through the wing of his jet.
As a test pilot in the California desert he flew the X-15, a rocket plane that reached the edge of space.

On Gemini 8 in 1966 he made the first docking of two spacecraft. Then a stuck thruster set the capsule spinning about once a second. Close to blacking out, he regained control and brought the crew home.

On 20 July 1969 he steered the lunar module Eagle past a field of boulders and landed on the Moon with seconds of fuel to spare. Hours later he stepped onto the surface, calling it "one small step for man". Some 600 million people watched.
He and Buzz Aldrin spent about two and a half hours walking on the Moon. With no wind there, their footprints are probably still there.

He never cashed in on his fame. He taught engineering at a university in Cincinnati and lived quietly on a farm in Ohio. When his barber sold his hair clippings to a collector, he threatened to sue. He died in 2012.
Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon, the boldest adventure of the 20th century.
pts: First person to walk on the Moon
Landed Apollo 11 with seconds of fuel to spare
Made the first docking in space
